## Motivation & Research Question 💟

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) results from the cumulative and reinforcing effects of biological, behavioral, and lifestyle factors over time.

-   How do demographic factors and health factors impact the probability that an individual will experience a heart attack?
-   We will examine **race, sex, age, smoking, drinking, diabetes, asthma, kidney disease, skin cancer, stroke,** and **general health** as predictors.
-   **Data Source:** Indicators of Heart Disease (2022) from Kaggle

. . .

## A Note on Self-Reporting

As some responses from this survey data are self-reported, variables like 
`general_health` may be subject to bias, though the massive $n$ helps stabilize 
these trends.

## Logistic Regression Model


$$log(Odds_{i}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1Smoking_i + \beta_2Alcohol_i + \beta_3Stroke_i + \\
\beta_3MentalHealth_i + \beta_4DiffWalking_i + \beta_5Sex_i + \\
\beta_6Over55_i + \beta_7Asian_i + \beta_8Black_i + \beta_9Hispanic_i + \\
\beta_{10}Diabetic_i + \beta_{11}HealthFair_i + \beta_{12}HealthGood_i + \\
\beta_{13}HealthExcellent_i + \beta_{14}Asthma_i + \beta_{15}KidneyDisease_i + \\
\beta_{16}SkinCancer_i$$


::: callout-note
## Model Selection

Best subset, forward, and backward selection all converged on the same predictors
for heart disease, optimizing for BIC.
:::

::: callout-note
## Model Assumptions

Caution: The dataset exhibits a class imbalance for the number of individuals with vs without
heart disease (less than 10% have heart disease)! All other logistic regression assumptions
were satisfied.
:::

## Key Predictors of Heart Attack Risk

::::: columns
::: {.column width="20%"}
**Findings:**

1.  Weight has the strongest negative impact.

2.  Manual transmissions tend to be more efficient.

3.  Horsepower has a smaller, but significant, effect.
:::

::: {.column width="80%"}

```{r}
#| include: false

set.seed(1234)

# 80% of data
n <-nrow(heartdisease)
train_indices <- sample(1:n, size = round(0.80 * n))

# add indices to data
heartdisease <- heartdisease %>% mutate(
  row_id = row_number(),
  set = ifelse(row_id %in% train_indices, "train", "test")
)

# filter train data
heart_train <- heartdisease %>% 
  filter(set == "train") %>% 
  select(-row_id, -set)

# filter test data
heart_test <- heartdisease %>% 
  filter(set == "test") %>% 
  select(-row_id, -set)
```


```{r}
#| include: false

# relevel the data to make sure that raceWhite is used as the baseline
heartdisease$race <- relevel(factor(heartdisease$race), ref = "White")
heartdisease$gen_health <- relevel(factor(heartdisease$gen_health), ref = "Poor")

heart_train$race <- relevel(factor(heart_train$race), ref = "White")
heart_train$gen_health <- relevel(factor(heart_train$gen_health), ref = "Poor")


final_log_reg <- glm(
  heart_disease ~  smoking + alcohol_drinking + stroke + mental_health + diff_walking + sex + age_category + race + diabetic + gen_health + asthma + kidney_disease + skin_cancer,
  data = heartdisease,
  family = "binomial"
)

```


```{r}

#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Coefficients of logistic regression model. Blue data points represent the additive effect of each predictor on the log-odds of heart disease. Red dashed line represents no effect on the log-odds of heart disease. Bars represent 95% confidence interval for the estimate. All effects are significant (p < 0.05) aside from the terms Mental Health, Native American, and Other Race."
#| label: fig-log-reg-coefficients
log_reg_tidy <- tidy(final_log_reg, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    term = case_match(term,
                     "alcohol_drinking1" ~ "Drinks Alcohol",
                     "mental_health" ~ "Mental Health",
                     "sex1" ~ "Male",
                     "age_category3" ~ "55 and older",
                     "raceAsian" ~ "Asian",
                     "raceHispanic" ~ "Hispanic",
                     "diabetic1" ~ "Diabetic",
                     "gen_healthGood" ~ "Good Health",
                     "asthma1" ~ "Asthma",
                     "skin_cancer1" ~ "Skin Cancer",
                     "smoking1" ~ "Smoker",
                     "stroke1" ~ "Stroke",
                     "diff_walking1" ~ "Difficulty Walking",
                     "age_category2" ~ "35-54 years old",
                     "raceAmerican Indian/Alaskan Native" ~ "Native American",
                     "raceBlack" ~ "Black",
                     "raceOther" ~ "Other Race",
                     "gen_healthFair" ~ "Fair Health",
                     "gen_healthExcellent" ~ "Excellent Health",
                     "kidney_disease1" ~ "Kidney Disease",
                     .default = term
                     ),
    term = reorder(term, estimate)
  )

ggplot(log_reg_tidy, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Effect on log-odds of heart disease (with 95% confidence interval)",
    y = NULL
  ) + 
  theme_classic()

```
